body:
## Problem

1.8.0 shipped `adlc gate-manifest enable`, which makes forest mode reachable for the first time. It does not ship rails-guard's forest awareness: `packages/rails-guard/lib/ci/manifest.mjs` returns 0 matches for `manifest.d|segment|anchor`, so the CI gate reads only `.adlc/manifest.jsonl`.

Consequence: once a repository is in forest mode, all new evidence is written to `.adlc/manifest.d/*.jsonl` — files the gate never opens. The append-only protection `assertAppendOnly` gives the root does not exist for segments. A PR can rewrite, truncate, reorder, or delete any committed segment file and CI raises nothing.

This is not a regression: forest mode never had CI guarding, so no operator has lost a guarantee they previously held, and it is opt-in. The defect is that **`enable` does not say so.** It returns `{decision: 'greenfield', markerPath, marker}` and the CLI prints that object; nothing in the success path mentions CI at all. An operator adopting the feature gets a working activation and no signal that their committed evidence is unguarded in PRs — they cannot make an informed choice about a tradeoff they were never shown.

The real fix is T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 6 (spec §9.1–9.3), a trust-root build. This ticket is the interim disclosure so the gap is visible while that lands, and it is expected to be REMOVED by slice 6.

## What to build

Disclose the limitation at the two places an operator meets it: the command output and the docs.

1. **`planEnable`/`enable` attach a machine-readable warning** whenever the repository is or becomes segmented — i.e. on the `greenfield` decision and on `already-enabled`. Both states mean segments are being written; both need the disclosure.

   The warning must be a structured value carrying a **stable identifier**, e.g. `warnings: [{ code: 'ci-cannot-guard-segments', message: '...' }]`. The code is the contract; the message is human text.

   Tests MUST assert on the `code`, never on the message prose. This repo's mutation gate mutates string literals, so a test pinned to the exact sentence turns every future wording improvement into a red gate for no behavioral reason. Assert presence, code, and placement — not wording.

2. **The CLI surfaces it in both modes.** `--json` output includes the warnings in the single JSON document it already emits (the existing "exactly ONE JSON document on stdout, in every mode" property must hold — do not print a second document or write the warning to stdout alongside JSON). Human mode prints it visibly.

3. **Nothing else changes.** The decision string, the exit code, and whether anything is written must all be identical to today. This is disclosure only. An operator's automation keying on `decision` must not break.

4. **`docs/tools/gate-manifest.md`** gains a short, plainly-worded note under the `enable` documentation: rails-guard cannot yet validate `.adlc/manifest.d/` segment files; segment tampering in a PR is not currently detected by CI; this closes when the forest CI gate lands. Do not overstate it as a vulnerability in a guarantee that was previously held — it never was.

## Acceptance criteria

All tests in `packages/gate-manifest/test/enable.test.mjs`, run with `node --test packages/gate-manifest/test/enable.test.mjs`. Write each test first and observe it FAIL before implementing.

1. **Greenfield carries the warning.** A greenfield fixture returns a `warnings` array containing an entry whose `code` is `ci-cannot-guard-segments`. Assert the code, not the message.
2. **Already-enabled carries the warning.** A fixture already in forest mode returns the same warning code.
3. **Disclosure follows SEGMENTATION, not the decision.** The original framing of this criterion — that no refusal may carry the warning — was wrong, and the build proved it: `planEnable` returns `refuse-ignored` from inside `if (isSegmentedRepo(dir))` when ignore rules drift after activation, and the CLI's keyless precheck returns before `enable()` runs at all. Both describe a repository in forest mode, writing unguarded segments right now. So a refusal MUST carry the warning when the repository is segmented (`refuse-ignored` on an already-active repo; `refuse-keyless` on a segmented repo, detected by bounded no-follow reads), and MUST NOT when it is not (`refuse-live-root`, `refuse-ignored` on a greenfield repo, the no-workspace refusal, the symlink refusals, and any keyless refusal on a single-file repo). Test every refusal variant explicitly against this contract — the point stands that a warning on every outcome would be noise that trains operators to ignore warnings.
4. **The decision and write behavior are unchanged.** For each decision path, `decision` and `written` are byte-identical to the pre-change values. Assert explicitly rather than by inspection.
5. **`--json` emits exactly one JSON document**, and it contains the warning. Verify by capturing stdout from the real bin and `JSON.parse`-ing the whole of it — a second document makes this throw, which is the point.
6. **Human mode prints the warning visibly.** Capture stdout from the bin without `--json` and assert the warning code or an unambiguous marker appears. Do not assert the sentence.
7. **No test asserts warning prose.** Verified by review of the diff; a test containing a full sentence from the message fails this criterion.
8. **Docs updated** — `docs/tools/gate-manifest.md` contains the note in the `enable` section.
9. **Full suite green:** `npm test` exits 0.

## Constraints

- `docs/specs/segmented-gate-manifest.md` and `docs/adr/0015-segmented-gate-manifest.md` are RAILED by T-MANIFEST-FOREST. Do not edit them. The normative spec is unchanged by this ticket; this is operator-facing disclosure only.
- `packages/gate-manifest/lib/record.mjs` is railed by T-01KYZ0C7BB3BD36J0MKAA110PV and `packages/gate-manifest/lib/spend.mjs` by T152. Neither needs to change.
- `packages/gate-manifest/**` is trust-root tier: P5 requires a distinct-provider `cross-model-review` approve bound to the reviewed revision before merge.

## Out of scope

- Implementing the forest CI gate (T-MANIFEST-FOREST slice 6) — that is the real fix and this warning is removed by it.
- Making rails-guard deny on an unguardable `.adlc/manifest.d/`. Considered and rejected: it would break CI for exactly the operators who adopted forest mode, with no remedy but downgrading or waiting out the slice-6 build, and it would fire late on an unrelated PR.
- Any change to `enable`'s decision logic, refusal set, or the activation marker.
title: gate-manifest enable must disclose that CI cannot yet guard segment files
